Q: Good morning. This is the adjuster following up on the claim. This call is being recorded with your permission. Can
you confirm you're comfortable with that?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Thank you. Please describe in your own words what happened on the day of the collision.
A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, in the right lane, and I wanted to move over to the left lane because I
needed to make a turn a little further up. I checked my mirror, I think, and I signaled. When I staretd to move over, a
car in the left lane came up alongside me and clipped the side of my vehicle. It scraped along the passenger side,
and I felt my car push toward the median.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you began your lane change?
A: Not clearly. I glanced over my shoulder but I didn't see anything right next to me. It must have been in my blind
spot.
Q: Did you stop after the contact, or did you keep going?
A: I pulled onto the shoulder as soon as I could get control of the car. The other driver stopped a little ahead of me
and we got out and talked for a few minutes.
Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?
A: My right wrist was hurting quite a bit, but I didn't think it was broken at first. I went to the emergency room later that
afternoon and they told me it was a fracture. I've been wearing a splint and I have a follow-up with a hand specialist
next week.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you think I should know about the collision?
A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get the repairs done and get my wirst taken care of.
Q: Understood. Thank you for your time today. We'll be in touch with next steps.
A: Okay, thank you.
</page>
